slot.brief: Evaluate a determinant whose entries are expressions by splitting rows into sums and factoring out common factors.

stem: If a, b, c are distinct real numbers, then the value of det [[a, b, c], [a^2, b^2, c^2], [b+c, c+a, a+b]] is

verdicts.working: Add row 1 to row 3, giving [?](a+b+c)(1,1,1)[?]. Factoring out [?]a+b+c[?], the determinant is [?](a+b+c)(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)[?].

working:
Add the first row to the third row: R3 -> R3 + R1. Then det = det [[a, b, c], [a^2, b^2, c^2], [a+b+c, a+b+c, a+b+c]]. Factor a+b+c from the third row: det = (a+b+c) det [[a, b, c], [a^2, b^2, c^2], [1, 1, 1]]. Reorder rows to get the Vandermonde form det [[1, 1, 1], [a, b, c], [a^2, b^2, c^2]] = (b-a)(c-a)(c-b) = (a-b)(b-c)(c-a). Hence the determinant is (a+b+c)(a-b)(b-c)(c-a), option A.

Independent check: Add row 1 to row 3, giving [?](a+b+c)(1,1,1)[?]. Factoring out [?]a+b+c[?], the determinant is [?](a+b+c)(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)[?].
solution:
Apply $R_3\to R_3+R_1$ and factor out $a+b+c$ from the third row:
$$D=(a+b+c)\begin{vmatrix}a&b&c\\a^2&b^2&c^2\\1&1&1\end{vmatrix}.
$$Reordering the rows to Vandermonde form gives $(b-a)(c-a)(c-b)=(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)$. Hence $D=(a+b+c)(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)$.
